newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK MIXED ON CURRENCIES.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS WEEK MIXED ON CURRENCIES.

text.p: Trade on Zimbabwe's interbank foreign exchange market got off to a quiet start on Monday with the local unit quoted mixed against hard currencies.
"Nothing at all has happened so far today," one dealer said.
"The market seems to be quite long at the moment and I haven't heard of any payments coming up -- so we may trade in the same ranges the whole day."

At around 0720 GMT, the Zimbabwe dollar was trading at 10.8150/8300 against the key U.S. unit, where it finished on Friday, but was quoted marginally softer against sterling at 18.3270/3580 compared to 18.3200/3400.
It was at 2.2920/2970 from 2.2900/3100 versus South Africa's rand but gained on the mark to 6.9000/9100 from 7.0200/0400, reflecting a stronger U.S. dollar on the German unit overseas.
